beats.say: An agent that can act inside your web app needs authority. Today that means an API key: every record, every field, valid until somebody remembers to revoke it.
But nobody means forever, everything. What a person actually means is narrow. These two accounts, these two fields, the next ten minutes.
Nothing turns that sentence into that grant. Mandate compiles it, into a WebMCP tool schema the agent reads and a rule the server enforces on every call.

beats.caption: Relay CRM — the host application
beats.say: This is Relay CRM. Ordinary business software. Mandate is not part of it. It's a capability layer installed into it, and right now it is doing nothing.

beats.caption: Selection proposes. It grants nothing.
beats.say: Selecting proposes a scope. It grants nothing. Two accounts picked, and the inspector still shows only the two read-only tools. Nothing appeared.

beats.caption: The human delegates: 2 accounts, 2 fields, 10 minutes
beats.say: Now the human delegates. These accounts, these two fields, ten minutes.

beats.caption: document.modelContext.registerTool(...)
beats.say: Three things change together. The rows take the authority ring. The panel states the exact scope, counting down. And the browser registers a tool that did not exist a second ago, whose schema is a readout of what the human just decided.

beats.caption: executeTool(mandate_stage_customer_update, { c-northwind, status })
beats.say: The agent calls it, through the browser's own WebMCP API. The change is staged, marked as the agent's. Nothing is committed.

beats.caption: executeTool(... { c-kestrel }) → OUT_OF_SCOPE
beats.say: Now ask that tool for an account that was selected but never delegated. Refused. Out of scope, decided by the server.

beats.caption: executeTool(... { c-atlas, field: arr }) → OUT_OF_SCOPE
beats.say: These notes contain a pasted email telling the assistant to approve everything. Run exactly the call it asks for. Refused. Authority does not come from text.

beats.caption: Narrowed mid-flight → mandate v2
beats.say: Narrow the mandate mid-flight. That publishes version two. The agent still believes in version one. Refused: policy changed. The schema was a courtesy. This is the enforcement.

beats.caption: Revoked → NO_ACTIVE_MANDATE
beats.say: Revoke it. The same call gets a different refusal: no active mandate. Two refusals, two reasons, both from the server.

beats.caption: There is no apply tool, and no route behind one
beats.say: And the most consequential act has no agent path at all. There is no apply tool, and no route behind one.

beats.caption: Only a human applies
beats.say: The human validates, and applies. The values land in the CRM.

beats.caption: The same session, without the instrumentation
beats.say: Everything you have just seen — the inspector, the caller, the audit — is instrumentation for this explanation. Here is the product underneath. The grant, the work, and the human commit. Enforcement is identical; only the panels are gone.

beats.caption: Human intent, compiled into a live WebMCP contract
beats.say: Shut the layer, and Relay CRM is an ordinary CRM again. Mandate turns explicit, temporary human intent into a live WebMCP contract that the server enforces on every call.
